title: Ben Gurion Airport to fully reopen as Israel lifts flight restrictions after ceasefire
byline: The Transportation Ministry announced that Israel will fully reopen the country’s airspace and resume regular operations at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport starting at midnight Wednesday-Thursday, roughly one day after a ceasefire was announced between the US, Israel and Iran.

title: Northern Line train services resume
byline: Train services on the Northern Line, which were disrupted following Cyclone Ditwah, resumed this morning (09), according to Sri Lanka Railways.

title: Suspect arrested in Ganemulla with large haul of heroin and ICE
byline: An individual has been arrested in Ganemulla along with a stock of heroin and crystal methamphetamine (Ice) believed to belong to an organized large-scale drug trafficker.

title: Bahrain and several other countries reopen airspace after US-Iran ceasefire agreement
byline: Syria, Iraq and Bahrain announced the reopening of their airspace Wednesday following the announcement of a ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran, according to civil aviation authorities.

title: Power outages reported in several areas
byline: Power outages have been reported in several parts of the island yesterday (08), affecting multiple areas due to a technical failure.

title: US ‘achieved every single objective’ in the Iran war, White House says
byline: The White House has reaffirmed its claims to have “achieved every single objective” set out since the start of the Iran war.

title: Iran says peace talks would be ‘unreasonable’ following Israeli strikes on Lebanon
byline: Israel pounded Lebanon with its heaviest strikes yet on Wednesday (Apr 8), killing hundreds of people and drawing a threat of retaliation from Iran, which suggested it would be “unreasonable” to proceed with talks to forge a permanent peace deal with the United States.

title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes killed 182 people and injured 890 others
byline: Lebanon’s Health Ministry said Wednesday that Israeli strikes across multiple parts of the country, including the capital, Beirut, have killed at least 182 people, according to an updated death toll.

title: GMOA to launch 48-hour token strike from 8am
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has announced that it will begin a 48-hour nationwide token strike starting from 8:00 a.m. today (09).

title: Showers expected after 2pm in several areas today
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at a few places in Western, Sabaragamuwa and Northwestern provinces and in Galle, Matara, Kandy, Nuwara-Eliya and Mannar districts after 2.00 p.m.

title: Donald Trump blasts NATO after closed-door Rutte meeting
byline: US President Donald Trump bashed NATO and appeared to renew his threats over Greenland after a closed-door meeting with alliance chief Mark Rutte, during which he was expected to discuss possibly leaving the pivotal security bloc.

title: Man arrested with conch shell in Kalutara
byline: An individual has been arrested for the possession of a conch shell (Valampuri) near the Kalutara depot.

title: Sri Lankan Australian playwright Shakthi wins Windham-Campbell Prize
byline: Sri Lankan Australian playwright S Shakthidharan, widely known as Shakthi, has won the $US175,000 ($250,000) Windham-Campbell Prize for drama.

title: Australia says Lebanon must be included in Middle East ceasefire
byline: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told reporters Thursday that the two-week ceasefire announced this week ‘‘is an important step forward.’’

title: Holy sites in Jerusalem reopens
byline: Israeli police announced that holy sites in Jerusalem will reopen to visitors and worshippers on Thursday morning.

title: JD Vance says Iran would be foolish to let talks collapse over Lebanon
byline: United States Vice President JD Vance has warned Iran that it would be “dumb” to jeopardise its ceasefire with Washington over Israel’s attacks in Lebanon.

title: Oil prices surge as investors remain wary of US-Iran ceasefire
byline: Oil prices rose on Thursday on investors’ concerns supply from the key Middle East producing region may not fully resume amid doubts the two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran will hold and as the crucial Strait of Hormuz remains restricted.

title: Youth arrested with over 1kg of ICE in Maradana
byline: A youth has been arrested for the possession of 1 kilogram and 220 grams of crystal methamphetamine (Ice) during a special raid conducted in Maradana.

title: IGP bans gifts and external funding for New Year events; allocates Rs. 250 per officer
byline: The Inspector General of Police, Priyantha Weerasuriya has issued a set of instructions to all police officers regarding the acceptance of gifts and the provision of monetary allowances for New Year celebrations.

title: 182 killed, 890 injured in Israeli strikes in Lebanon
byline: Lebanon’s Health Ministry said Wednesday that Israeli strikes across multiple parts of the country, including the capital, Beirut, have killed at least 182 people, according to an updated death toll.

title: Iran tells ships how to avoid mines in Strait of Hormuz - state media
byline: Ships planning to pass through the Strait of Hormuz should take alternative routes, to “comply with the principles of maritime safety and to be protected from possible collisions with sea mines”, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said in a statement cited in Iranian state media.

title: President reiterates government’s commitment to alleviating rural poverty
byline: The 59th Aluth Sahal Mangallaya or the National New Rice Festival commenced today (09) at the sacred Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: US military will remain around Iran until Tehran complies with deal: Trump
byline: US President Donald Trump said all U.S. ships, aircraft, and military personnel would stay in place in and around Iran until it fully complied with a deal.

title: Hezbollah fires rockets at Israel in first attack since ceasefire
byline: Hezbollah, Iran’s proxy militia in Lebanon, said early Thursday it fired rockets at northern Israel in response to Israeli ceasefire violations, in its first attack since the deal was reached, Reuters news agency reported.

title: EU urges shift from ‘fragile’ US-Iran ceasefire to permanent peace during Riyadh mission
byline: Vice-President of the European Commission (EU) Kaja Kallas arrived in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, for a high-stakes diplomatic push to transform a temporary two-week truce between the United States and Iran into a lasting regional settlement.

title: Kudawa entrance to Sinharaja Reserve closed for six days
byline: The Kudawa Entrance of the Sinharaja Forest Reserve will be closed for six days from tomorrow (10) until April 15, the Sinharaja Forest Reserve Controller’s Office announced.

title: Nepal issues arrest warrant for ex-PM Deuba in graft probe
byline: Nepal has issued an arrest warrant for former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba for alleged corruption, officials said on Thursday (Apr 9), making him the latest high-profile figure targeted under the new government.

title: 12-hour water cut announced for Homagama and Pelenwatta
byline: A 12-hour water cut will be imposed in the Homagama and Pelenwatta areas today (09) and tomorrow (10) due to the prevailing dry weather conditions, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) announced.

title: Health Minister cancels scheduled meeting with GMOA
byline: Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa has announced that the discussion scheduled for today (09) with the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) will not be held.

title: Iran warns US must choose between ceasefire and war via Israel, ‘it cannot have both’
byline: Iran warned on Wednesday that the US must choose between a ceasefire and ‘‘continued war via Israel,’‘ saying Washington ‘‘cannot have both."

title: Man arrested with conch shell in Kalutara
byline: An individual has been arrested for the possession of a conch shell (Valampuri) near the Kalutara depot.

title: President reiterates commitment to alleviating rural poverty
byline: The 59th Aluth Sahal Mangallaya or the National New Rice Festival commenced today (09) at the sacred Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: IMF reaches staff-level agreement on fifth and sixth reviews of Sri Lanka’s EFF
byline: Sri Lanka and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached staff-level agreement on economic policies to conclude the combined Fifth and Sixth Reviews of Sri Lanka’s reform program supported by the IMF’s Extended Fund Facility.

title: Sri Lankan woman injured following Israel strikes in Lebanon
byline: A Sri Lankan woman has reportedly sustained minor injuries following airstrikes carried out by Israel on Lebanon yesterday (08).

title: Iranian negotiators head to Pakistan - despite skepticism over ‘repeated ceasefire violations’
byline: An Iranian delegation is heading to Pakistan today to begin negotiations with the US on ending the war, Iran’s ambassador to Pakistan has confirmed.

title: Ex-President Ranil Wickremesinghe returns to the island
byline: Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe, who underwent a surgery in Singapore, has returned to the island this morning (09).

title: Over 200,000 SMEs ceased operations between 2018–2022, says Deputy Minister
byline: More than 200,000 micro, small, and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) in Sri Lanka ceased operations between 2018 and 2022 due to various reasons, the Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning, Dr. Anil Jayantha said.

title: Netanyahu warns Israel will continue to strike Hezbollah ‘wherever necessary’
byline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel will continue to strike Hezbollah ‘‘wherever necessary’’, following a ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran.

title: UK deployed military to deter Russian submarines from its waters
byline: Britain deployed its armed forces to deter Russian submarines from attacking its cables and pipelines when they spent around a month in British waters earlier this year, defence minister John Healey said on Thursday.

title: Public urged to control blood sugar levels during festive season
byline: The general public has been urged by medical professionals to take steps to control blood sugar levels during the Sinhala and Tamil New Year festive season.

title: Tom Holland says new Spider-Man film will add more humour and ‘fun’ elements
byline: Actor Tom Holland has revealed that the ‘‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’‘ film did some additional photography recently to add in ‘‘more humor’‘ and beef up a ‘‘villain plotline’‘ despite officially wrapping up production last year.

title: Easter Sunday attacks a conspiracy planned since 2017 – Public Security Minister
byline: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala has claimed that ongoing investigations have uncovered that the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks were not an isolated incident, but a result of a conspiracy that had been in motion since 2017.

title: Met. Department warns of possible extended drought if El Niño develops
byline: The Department of Meteorology has indicated that an El Niño event during the southwest monsoon season could result in drought conditions extending through September.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for most parts of the country
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for tomorrow (10) for residents of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Eastern, North-Western, Northern and North-Central provinces and in Monaragala District.

title: Colombo Fort Railway Station modernization project launched
byline: The modernization project of the Colombo Fort Railway Station was officially launched today (09), with Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya presiding over the inauguration.

title: SLC to file objections to Nuwan Thushara’s petition over non-issuance of NOC
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket has informed the Colombo District Court that it intends to file objections to a petition submitted by cricketer Nuwan Thushara over the non-issuance of a “No Objection Certificate” (NOC) to participate in the 2026 Indian Premier League.

title: More than 3,000 Iranians killed during war, medical body says
byline: More than 3,000 people were killed throughout Iran during the war that ⁠began on February 28, Iran’s forensic chief told state media on Thursday, adding ⁠that 40% of the dead needed forensic ⁠work to be identified and ⁠returned to families.

title: Govt’s policy is to build a sustainable public transport system – PM
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya emphasized that the government’s policy is to build a sustainable transport system that enables children, women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities to access services conveniently.

title: Extension of State of Public Emergency passed in Parliament
byline: The motion to approve the extension of the State of Public Emergency under the Public Security Ordinance was passed in Parliament today (9) by a majority of 110 votes.

title: Islamabad under security lockdown for US-Iran talks; two-day public holiday declared
byline: Pakistan’s capital has been placed under tight security lockdown as it prepares to host the first round of direct negotiations between the United States and Iran, scheduled to begin on April 10, reported Pakistan’s state media on Thursday.

title: Govt has comprehensive plan to elevate living standards of farmers – President
byline: The National New Rice Festival, a traditional annual ceremony in which newly harvested rice from the Maha season is offered to the sacred Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi, was held this morning (09) under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in the presence of the historic Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi in Anuradhapura.

title: British Airways cuts Middle East flights, shifts capacity to Asia and Africa
byline: British Airways said on Thursday it will cut flights to the Middle East when services resume, permanently drop Jeddah as a destination, while adding capacity to India and Africa, as heightened regional tensions disrupt schedules and weigh on demand.

title: Ministry urges schools not to burden parents with excessive event expenses
byline: The Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education says that there have been reports of excessive spending on events and various celebrations organized in schools.

title: Sri Lanka repatriates 125 telecom fraud suspects to China
byline: Sri Lankan police recently repatriated 125 individuals suspected of involvement in telecom fraud, who had been apprehended during earlier crackdown operations, to China, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security (MPS) said on Thursday.
